deepdive.sec: Diversified Retail NBFC / Vehicle + MSME + Gold Finance

bull_bear.body: Post ~INR39,600cr April-2026 raise, the quarter's priority was **deleveraging** — ~INR18,000cr of high-cost liabilities repaid (leverage 3.82x→2.14x, CAR 34.1%). That phase is now "done": no further repayment; surplus liquidity (kept ~3 months / ~INR17,000-18,000cr of repayment cover) to be deployed into growth over ~1-1.5 months, then fresh borrowing including securitization/direct-assignment resumes. Off-balance-sheet share fell simply because no securitization was done this quarter (not demand-led).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Monsoon/El-Nino:** seasonal rainfall ~24% below normal (Jun 4-Jul 16); management explicitly **waiting for Q2** to judge rural-income/agri-output impact before confirming the 18% guide — the key swing factor.
- **West-Asia war / fuel:** feared steep fuel-price spike didn't materialise; one-time cost pass-through "already absorbed"; E20 ethanol norm reduces import dependence. Residual risk if retail fuel spikes further.
- **NIM normalisation:** structural glide to 8.5% as new-vehicle mix rises — near-term supported by surplus capital, but the ~INR500cr capital-NII tailwind fades.
- **Asset quality:** GS3 nudged up (4.58%→4.64%; +18% YoY in Stage-3 assets flagged by an analyst) — management calls it seasonal, not stress; gold Stage-2/3 forward-flows to watch (bullet→interest-servicing migration).
- **E20 durability** debate on used cars — management downplays (OEMs certify E20; SFL finances cars <7yr, trucks unaffected).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and deliberately conservative — repeatedly defers full-year upgrades to post-Q2 monsoon clarity while expressing comfort on demand. Transparent on the capital-raise mechanics (deleveraging first, growth next) and willing to be pushed on the 8.5% NIM guide without caving. Macro-heavy opening (GDP/inflation/auto volumes) frames the cyclical tailwind. IR-responsive (offers offline data splits).
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- The quarter's optics are a **capital-raise artefact**: ~INR500cr of NII, the leverage collapse to 2.14x, the 34.1% CAR and part of the 9% NIM all trace to the April infusion — normalise for it before trend-lining PAT/NIM.
- **Deleveraging, not slow growth, explains falling liabilities/off-book** — a temporary, now-complete phase; expect borrowing + securitization to resume from quarter-end (a re-leveraging growth signal).
- The **8.5% medium-term NIM guide is a choice** (pass funding benefit to borrowers to win new-vehicle share), not a forced compression — the real question is mix-shift speed (new-vehicle 16%→30%+).
- **Gold + MSME are the mix-changers**: both guided to grow faster than the 18% average, gradually diversifying SFL away from its CV core.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- MUFG preferential issue: 471,121,055 fully paid-up equity shares of Rs. 2 face value at Rs. 840.93 per share (premium Rs. 838.93) aggregating Rs. 39,617.98 crores, representing 20% of post-issue equity share capital on a fully diluted basis; allotted April 08, 2026 after shareholder approval on January 14, 2026, with MUFG becoming "a minority public shareholder".
- Deployment of those proceeds: during the quarter ended June 30, 2026, Rs. 37,451.22 crores have been utilised and unutilised proceeds of Rs. 2,166.76 crores were invested in liquid mutual funds; a Regulation 32 statement confirms no deviation/variation in utilisation of the preferential-issue funds.
- Balance-sheet reset from the raise: net worth Rs. 108,297.48 crores at June 30, 2026 versus Rs. 65,244.09 crores at March 31, 2026; debt-equity ratio 2.14 times versus 3.82 times; total debts to total assets 0.67 versus 0.78.
- Dividend: final equity dividend of 300% i.e. Rs. 6 per share for FY2025-26 aggregating Rs. 14,117,490,768 (gross) paid on July 21, 2026, in addition to an interim dividend of Rs. 4.80 per share (240%) declared October 31, 2025 — "the total dividend for the financial year 2025-26 is Rs. 10.80 per equity share".
- Funding plan: the Board approved a periodical resource mobilisation plan for issuance of debt securities (redeemable NCDs / subordinated debentures, bonds/notes) on private placement and/or public issue, in one or more tranches, onshore/offshore, from August 1, 2026 to October 31, 2026.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **Commercial Vehicles (core):** INR19,556cr disbursed; growth "in line with ~20% market" — used-CV demand from rural market strong; no vehicle idling / stress seen despite fuel worries.
- **New vehicle:** ~16% of disbursement and rising — driven by existing-customer upgrades and win-back of customers lost when SFL couldn't match rates (now can, on lower funding cost + capital).
- **Passenger Vehicles:** INR11,018cr.
- **Gold:** INR5,153cr; ~2.5% of book, 2,200 branches enabled; targeted to double to ~5% in 3 years (see §6).
- **MSME:** INR6,184cr; ~15% of book, historically South-concentrated, now rolling out West→North/East (hub-and-spoke processing). Inflection underway; growth to beat company average.
- **2-Wheelers** INR3,548cr; **Personal Loans** INR2,773cr (kept within known customers, limited outsourcing); **Farm** INR947cr; **Construction Equipment** INR792cr.

business.body:
- Segment structure: "The Company is primarily engaged in the business of financing and there are no separate reportable segments identified as per Ind AS 108 - Operating segments. The Company operates in a single geographical segment i.e. domestic."
- Regulatory identity: the Company is "registered under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 as Non-Banking Financial Company", which is why most Regulation 52(4) ratios (DSCR, ISCR, current ratio, debtors/inventory turnover, operating margin) are disclosed as "NA".
- Group perimeter for the consolidated results: Shriram Finance Limited (Holding Company), Shriram Overseas Investment Limited (100%, subsidiary from May 09, 2025) and Shriram Automall India Limited (44.56%, associate). Bharath Investment Pte. Ltd. was a step-down subsidiary only from May 09, 2025 to March 11, 2026.
- Consolidation note: the Company, its subsidiary and associate "are primarily engaged in the business of financing and other incidental facilitating activities", so no separate reportable segments are identified at group level either.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Divestment] Shriram Overseas sold its entire 81.63% stake in Bharath Investments Pte. Ltd., Singapore — 755,146 equity shares transferred for a consideration of Rs. 1.58 crores on March 11, 2026; BIPL ceased to be a step-down subsidiary and the resultant loss of Rs. 0.51 crores is presented under discontinued operations.
- [Secured debt] Secured non-convertible debentures of Rs. 33,021.82 crores as on June 30, 2026 are secured by assets under hypothecation loan agreements plus exclusive charge and mortgage of immovable property; security cover available on secured NCDs is 1.09 times, and the Company confirms compliance with the covenants in the disclosure documents.
- [Labour Codes] The four New Labour Codes became effective November 21, 2025 with rules notified May 08, 2026; employee benefits expenses for the year ended March 31, 2026 include incremental impact on gratuity of Rs. 131.71 crores and on long-term compensated absences of Rs. 65.24 crores (standalone; Rs. 131.73 crores and Rs. 65.26 crores in the consolidated notes) due to the change in the definition of wages.
- [ESOP] During the quarter the Company allotted 228,702 equity shares of Rs. 2 face value at an exercise price of Rs. 38.71 per share (including premium of Rs. 36.71) under the Shriram Finance Limited Employee Stock Option Scheme 2023 (No. 1).
- [Audit] Joint statutory auditors M M NISSIM & CO LLP and G. D. Apte & Co. issued unmodified limited review conclusions on both the standalone and consolidated results; the March 31, 2026 quarter figures are balancing figures between audited full-year and reviewed nine-month numbers.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: NIM 9.04% is a capital-inflated peak; ~INR500cr of the NII is surplus-capital income that decays as liquidity is deployed. Management guides operational NIM to ~8.5% medium term — an analyst (Chintan) pushed back that this looks conservative given slow mix-shift; management held the line ("we've always been conservative"). Funding tailwind: incremental cost 7.77% vs 8.56% on-book; ratings-driven repricing benefit as SFL is no longer borrowed-for as an AA entity. Cost-to-income low at 25.48%; incremental branch/manpower cost to be absorbed by volume.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** PAT INR3,444.56cr (+59.8%); NII INR8,055.70cr (+33.7%); NIM 9.04% (peak, capital-aided); AUM INR3.14L cr (+15.3% YoY / +3.8% QoQ); disbursements INR49,974cr (+19.5%). GS3 4.64% / NS3 2.33%; credit cost 1.66%; C/I 25.48%. Post ~INR39,600cr April raise: leverage 2.14x (vs 3.82x), CAR 34.1%, LCR 262.54%, ~INR18,000cr liabilities repaid, ~INR500cr NII from surplus capital. Guidance: FY27 ~18% (Q2 ≥15%), NIM→8.5% medium term, credit cost ~2%, gold 2.5%→5% in 3yr, new-vehicle→30%+ book, MSME 15%→20%, ~150 branches.
- _Q2 FY27 → check: monsoon/rural-income verdict and whether 18% FY27 guide is upgraded/held; NIM trajectory as capital-NII (~INR500cr) fades toward 8.5%; resumption of borrowing/securitization; gold & MSME growth outpacing average; GS3 (seasonal vs stress); new-vehicle mix progress toward 20-25% disbursal._
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)

outlook.body:
- **AUM/loan growth:** **FY27 ~18%** (earlier guidance holds; will revise after Q2 once monsoon impact is clear). **Q2FY27 ≥15%**, accelerating in H2 if conditions improve.
- **NIM:** hold at ~current (~9%) for the immediate 2 quarters (capital deployment); **normalise to ~8.5% over the medium term (2-3 yr)** as lower-yield new-vehicle mix rises and cost benefit is passed to borrowers.
- **Credit cost:** ~**2%** near and medium term (currently running below at 1.66%).
- **Cost-to-income:** stable (branch/manpower adds absorbed by volume).
- **Gold book:** **double in 3 years, ~2.5%→~5% of book** (2,200 branches gold-enabled).
- **New-vehicle mix:** disbursement share 16%→20-25%; **new-vehicle book to 30%+** of total (medium term).
- **MSME:** ~15%→~20% of book; growth **above** the 18% company average.
- **CV:** ~15% growth for FY27.
- **Branches:** ~**150 added** in FY27.
- **Funding:** no further liability repayment; deploy surplus liquidity into growth over ~1-1.5 months, then resume fresh borrowing / securitization toward quarter-end.
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body: Not an order-book model — forward view keyed to auto sales + rural income. Q1FY27 industry volumes (management-cited): CV +14.1%, M&HCV +18.3%, LCV +20.8%, PV +25.9%, 2W +20.3%, 3W +29.7%, tractors +21.6%, construction equipment +8.8% (first positive after a negative FY). EV sales surged (2W +69.3%, PV +94.8%). GST rate cut is the demand catalyst. Disbursement pipeline healthy across segments; construction-equipment disbursal (~INR1,000cr for 5 quarters) expected to re-accelerate toward its old ~INR2,000cr run-rate from next quarter.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- **Gold-loan scale-up** — the clearest optionality: existing branch network repurposed (2,200 ready), riding the shift of borrowers from unsecured/hand-loans and pawnbrokers to gold-backed credit; target 2x book in 3 years.
- **MSME geographic expansion** beyond the South — long runway ("a lot of scope"), gated by hiring specialised manpower in North/Central.
- **New-vehicle penetration** of the existing customer base — larger ticket sizes structurally lift disbursement growth.
- **Cross-sell of personal loans** to gold/MSME customers (previously only 2-wheeler customers).

deepdive.thesis: A very strong, capital-flush quarter: PAT +59.8% to INR3,444.56cr, NII +33.7% to INR8,055.70cr and NIM at a peak 9.04%  — turbo-charged by the ~INR39,600cr equity infusion (April 2026) that added ~INR500cr of NII, cut leverage to 2.14x (from 3.82x) and lifted CAR to 34.1%. Disbursements +19.5% and AUM +15.3% YoY  on a GST-cut-driven auto up-cycle, with used/new-CV demand resilient despite the West-Asia war. Management reaffirms an **18% FY27 growth** guide , a medium-term normalisation of NIM to ~8.5% as new-vehicle mix rises, ~2% credit-cost, and outsized gold/MSME expansion. Asset quality stable . The one debate: whether the ~9% NIM can be held vs management's deliberately conservative 8.5% medium-term guide.
